policy_title: Increase local government funding and devolved powers
stated: Increase local government funding across England by £5bn per year. Give the Welsh Government the same devolved powers as the Scottish Government in advance of a new constitutional settlement, and support the Senedd if it decides to hold an independence referendum.

source.quote: Elected Greens will ensure that local authorities across England are given the powers and resources they need. They will push for an increase in local government funding of £5bn per year to tackle the current under-funding crisis. Elected Greens would give the Welsh Government the same devolved powers as the Scottish Government in advance of a new constitutional settlement. Elected Greens will support the Senedd if it decides to hold an independence referendum.

bearing_set.reason: Adult social care is the dominant unfunded pressure on English councils (~40% of budgets); a £5bn general uplift would produce a real, non-negligible verdict on social care access and later-life support.
Explicitly supporting a Welsh independence referendum is a direct democratic/voting-rights matter, falling squarely within O9's scope of democratic and voting rights.
Improved adult social care funding reduces NHS delayed-discharge pressures (bed-blocking), a concrete mechanism linking local government finance to NHS waiting-list capacity and access.

A £5bn/year recurring spending commitment is a material fiscal obligation; without a stated funding mechanism, it bears concretely on the funded-vs-borrowed balance and the sustainability of the debt path.

membership_note: Four genuine bearings: two service-delivery effects from the local-funding component (O8 primary, O3 secondary via public-health and discharge functions), one democratic-rights effect from the Welsh devolution/referendum commitment (O9), and one fiscal effect from the unfunded spending pledge (O12). Housing (O1) and children's services (O7) are plausible but too diffuse without allocation detail to clear the non-negligible bar independently.
